## Challenge

Measure a capacitor discharging through an LED or low-current active buzzer. Then show mathematically why an ordinary classroom capacitor cannot sustain an automotive horn.

## Safety boundary

- Student builds use protected extra-low voltage and a small approved load.
- Verify electrolytic polarity and voltage rating.
- Discharge through a resistor and verify voltage before handling.
- Never short the capacitor.
- A fused real horn is a teacher demonstration only.

## Pathways

| Minimum | Proficient | Extension |
|---|---|---|
| Calculate stored energy; record capacitor voltage and output change during discharge. | Add $\tau=RC$, a voltage-time graph, KVL/KCL, current estimate, and two-capacitance comparison. | Use the capacitor as a timing/control signal for an approved driver and relay while a separate supply powers the load. |

## Equations

$$E=\frac{1}{2}CV^2 \qquad i_C=C\frac{dv_C}{dt} \qquad C\approx\frac{I\Delta t}{\Delta V}$$

## Gates

1. Part type, value, rating, polarity, and load current approved.
2. Power-off schematic and discharge path approved.
3. Charge KVL check passes.
4. Discharge data table is complete.
5. Direct-horn estimate and limitations are explained.

## Submit

Two energy-flow models, approved schematic, parts table, calculations, voltage-time graph, KVL/KCL evidence, comparison test, safety decisions, and reflection.
